history.dynasty: Unknown; attributed by tradition to Parasurama (mythological). No evidence of exact construction date; building said to date to the 11th century and murals to the 15th-18th centuries (verify).
history.period: Treta Yuga per legend; structure medieval
history.summary: One of the oldest and most powerful Shiva temples in Kerala, held in reverence by both Shaivites and Vaishnavites. Legend: the demon Khara, after penance to Shiva at Chidambaram, received three lingams; the one held in his right hand was set down at Vaikom and entrusted to the sage Vyaghrapada, who attained darshan of Shiva and Parvati here under a peepal tree (commemorated by the Ashtami festival). The temple is famous for its oval sanctum (unique in Kerala) roofed with copper sheets, an 8-acre courtyard, four gopurams and a golden flagstaff. Believers hold that worshipping Vaikom, Ettumanoor and Kaduthuruthy before Ucha Pooja fulfils wishes. The temple was the epicentre of the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) temple-entry movement in which Mahatma Gandhi took part. Administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. NOTE: the temple's own site says no evidence establishes the exact date of construction.

name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Vaikom is a historic town in Kottayam district, Kerala, on the eastern banks of the Vembanad Lake and its backwaters. It is famous for the Vaikom Mahadeva Temple, the Vaikom Satyagraha temple-entry movement of 1924-25, and its serene waterways. The town lies roughly 30 km from Kottayam and is well connected by road to Ernakulam and Kottayam.

travel.road: KSRTC bus station on SH-15 (Ettumanoor-Ernakulam Highway); regular buses from Kottayam and Ernakulam (verify)
